item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-13: reverse-function
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (arg in `ecx`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: xor eax, eax jmp check top: mov edx, ecx dec edx and ecx, edx inc eax check: cmp ecx, 0 jne top ret ```
What does it return for 0, 1, 12 and 0xFF?
---
## Answer
```c int mystery(unsigned x) { int n = 0; while (x != 0) { x &= x - 1; // clear lowest set bit n++; } return n; // popcount: number of 1 bits } ```
Results: 0, 1, 2, 8.
## Explanation
- `jmp check` jumps straight to the test at the bottom, so the body can run zero times. That makes it a `while` loop, not `do/while`. Compilers often lay loops out this way. - `dec` subtracts 1 (`inc` adds 1). x-1 flips the lowest set bit and every 0 below it, so `x & (x-1)` clears exactly that one bit. For 12 (1100b): 1100 → 1000 → 0, two passes. - eax counts the passes, so the result is the number of set bits.
